summary: Rate adaptation misconfiguration causes cascading 5xx, circuit oscillation, and runtime memory pressure
description:
Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC BrightDesk reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for inference requests routed through us-east. Error rate spiked from ~0.2% to ~7% over 30 minutes. The pattern correlates with per-tenant rate adaptation behavior and a recent throttle configuration push to reduce noisy-tenant impact.

Impact: BrightDesk (dedicated) saw degraded throughput for chat and embedding routes; customer-reported elevated latency, partial responses, and spikes of 502/503/504. Customer-facing SLOs impacted; requests dropped and retries amplified error volume.

Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated pool for BrightDesk, models: gpt-open-13B and gpt-open-7B. Autoscaler group: ded-pool-3.

Steps to reproduce (observed in-prod):
1. Run sustained mixed chat+embedding synthetic load at BrightDesk steady-state QPS (~120 qps) while toggling the rate-adaptation window from 60s->15s (as pushed in config).
2. Observe gateway start returning 502s and increased hedged retries from clients at t+2m.
3. Serving runtimes begin OOM-like memory pressure logs and eviction traces at t+5m.

Relevant logs / metrics snippets:
- apigw: "priority_shim: shed_rate increased to 0.45 for tenant=brightdesk"
- apigw: "circuit: oscillation detected, trip_count=3, reopen_after=12s"
- runtime: "gpu_mem_pressure: free<reserved_threshold, attempt_prefetch=false"
- runtime: "kernel_watchdog: killing worker pid=23112 (oom suspected)"
- metrics: p50 latency drifted from 120ms->450ms, 5xx rate to 7.1% over 30m

Observed behavior: The shortened rate-adaptation window caused the API gateway to more aggressively shed connections for transient spikes. The shedding triggered hedged retries and client-side backoffs which, combined with aggressive prefetch cancellation, caused rapid fan-in to the serving runtime. Runtime KV cache thrashing and larger-than-expected per-request memory residency caused runtime workers to evict/panic, which surfaced as upstream 5xx. Circuit breakers on the gateway oscillated (tripped->reopened) repeatedly, amplifying error churn.

Immediate customer impact: BrightDesk reported multiple timeouts and incomplete chat completions between 14:15-15:10 UTC. Customer operations flagged incident to support; they paused background bulk embedding jobs as a workaround.
comments: 2026-03-12T14:25Z - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE and Eng. Collected initial request IDs and metrics dashboard link.
2026-03-12T14:40Z - Ravi Patel (SRE): Noted sudden rise in shed_rate after config sweep. Reproduced gateway circuit oscillation in staging with shortened rate window. Adding to investigation notes.

2026-03-12T15:05Z - Elena Voss (Oncall Runtime): Observed increased kernel watchdog restarts and OOM-like traces on ded-pool-3. Temporarily disabled the rate-adapt aggressive thresholds for BrightDesk which reduced error rate.
2026-03-12T15:25Z - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed partial recovery after temporary config rollback. Continued monitoring.
2026-03-13T09:12Z - Product Ops: Opening follow-up ticket to review default rate-adaptation rollout gating and canary size. Assigned to product infra.

2026-03-14T11:00Z - Ravi Patel (SRE): Draft mitigation applied: increased gate reopen_after to 30s, restored adaptive window to 60s, and pinned prefetch cancellation backoff. Monitoring shows 5xx back to baseline.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Shorter rate-adapt window caused over-eager shedding, creating retry amplification from clients and hedged retry fan-in.
Hypothesis B: Prefetch cancellation combined with shed traffic increased runtime KV cache churn and memory residency per request, leading to worker evictions.
Repro steps validated in staging by toggling rate-adapt window and firing mixed chat+embed workload. Circuit breaker metrics matched production pattern.

Found related config rollout PR earlier in the day: infra/pull/2401 which modified adaptive window default from 60->15s for aggressive tenants. Rollout was global by mistake; intended canary size was 10% but target selector omitted.
Telemetry: top noisy endpoints were chat.stream and embed.bulk_upload. Prefetch latency increased concurrently which matches cache invalidation traces.
Mitigation tested: rollback of adaptive window + gentle reopen_after increase reduced circuit oscillation and downstream OOMs in canary cluster.
resolution: Mitigated: rollback of the aggressive rate-adaptation change for BrightDesk and global pause of the rollout. Gateway thresholds adjusted (reopen_after 30s, min_window 45s). Runtime prefetch backoffs tuned and autoscaler warmup increased to reduce hot-spotting. Follow-ups: 1) revert PR infra/pull/2401 and reintroduce with strict canary gating; 2) add dashboard alarm for priority_shim shed_rate > 0.3; 3) postmortem doc and updated runbook entry for rate-adaptation rollouts.
